prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1210; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, involving two vehicles traveling in the same direction on a city street. Driver 1 was stopped at a signal when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear bumper. Driver 1 reported a wrist fracture and was transported for treatment. The reported injury is consistent with the type and force of this impact. Damage to both vehicles corresponds with the description given by the drivers, and no prior damage to either vehicle was known to those interviewed. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general positions of the vehicles and the location of the impact. No independent witnesses were located. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved. Driver 1 stated having been seated in the driver's position, although the passenger seat location was not clearly established during the interview and remains unclear from the available information. Passenger, who was in the front seat of Driver 1's vehicle, reported no injuries at the scene.
